The privacy report card of the most downloaded apps

490 Android apps graded from A to E on the permissions they ask for and the trackers they embed, with the same scoring engine as the VYLIA app and the public reports of Exodus Privacy.

0apps graded A among the 92 most downloaded
77%of the most downloaded graded D or E
35median score out of 100 (most downloaded)
11trackers per app on median, up to 36

These are maximum-exposure grades. Off the phone, nobody knows what you allowed: every declared permission is counted as granted. On your phone, VYLIA only fully counts the ones you granted. The grade there is often better, and the gap shows what you gain by refusing access. Trackers are in the code: they weigh the same everywhere. Example on a test phone, on 9 November 2026: Telegram goes from C (50) to B (83), Instagram from E (29) to C (51) and ChatGPT from D (39) to B (71), depending on the access granted.

The overall level is poor. Of the 74 most downloaded apps, 0 gets an A, 57 are graded D or E, and the median score tops out at 35 out of 100. 70 apps out of 74 embed at least one known tracker; Google Firebase Analytics is in 59 of them.

Games concentrate trackers. The 34 games in the list embed 20 of them on median, against 7 for the other apps: monetization and profiling kits that follow the player from one app to the next. Their grade sometimes stays average because they ask for few permissions (1 penalized on median).

Messaging and social apps: fewer trackers, more access. The 29 apps in these categories embed 4 trackers on median, but 9 penalized permissions: contacts, call log, location, microphone. This is where your settings matter most.

By category and by tracker. The gap between categories is clear: "health, admin" apps get a median score of 76, "reading, news" apps 12. The same trackers come up everywhere: Google Firebase Analytics is in 80% of third-party apps, Google CrashLytics in 58% and Google AdMob in 43%. 85% of apps embed at least one Google tool and 51% at least one Facebook kit: a few companies thus see data from a large share of your apps. Details at the bottom of the page.

Today's hits do no better. Among the 226 apps of the daily charts in France and the United States, the median score is 38 and 62% are graded D or E.

Phone makers' apps, often impossible to uninstall. They get a median score of 58. Among the makers with at least three reported apps, Google does best (76) and Transsion worst (19). These apps embed few known trackers but a lot of access: they are part of the system.

By contrast, the alternatives suggested by the VYLIA app get a median score of 95, and 32 out of 33 are graded A or B. A good grade is possible: it depends on design choices, not on the kind of app.

Reducing your exposure

A poor grade is not a fate. Your exposure surface, everything your apps can know about you, depends as much on your settings as on the apps themselves. Between an app that was granted everything and talks freely to its trackers, and the same app with limited access and filtered trackers, the gap is real.

1

Limit permissions

Refuse location, contacts, microphone or call log when the app does not need them. That is the gap between the grade in this ranking and the one on your phone: on a test phone, Telegram goes from C (50) to B (83) and ChatGPT from D (39) to B (71).

2

Filter trackers

Trackers are in the code: refusing access does not remove them. VYLIA's shield, a local anti-tracker VPN, stops them from reaching their servers, in every app, including the ones you keep. The score measures what the app embeds and does not change.

3

Remove unused apps

A forgotten app keeps its access and its trackers. VYLIA spots the ones you no longer open: uninstalling them reduces your exposure at no cost.

4

Switch to an alternative

For many uses, a more respectful app exists. The alternatives suggested by VYLIA get a median score of 95 in this ranking.

5

Use the web version

Many services work in the browser, installed like an app (WebAPK). The app and its trackers leave the phone, and the browser limits what the site can learn.

6

Pick the lighter version

The same app sometimes exists as a "Lite" or "Go" version, with its own code and therefore its own grade. Facebook Lite gets C (50) against E (0) for Facebook. For the same use, the exposure gain is immediate.

Method

  • Which apps. Sources: Wikipedia, List of most-downloaded Google Play applications (free apps from 500 million to 10 billion downloads); AppInsider for "Right now" (top 200 of the daily charts of free apps, France and the United States, 9 November 2026; when the app's grid does not know an app, its category comes from its Google Play category, for this ranking only); for "Google and phone makers", the apps of Google and phone makers found in those two sources; the alternatives of the VYLIA app available on Google Play. Apps from Google, Apple and phone makers (Samsung, Xiaomi, Huawei, Motorola, vivo, Oppo, Transsion) are ranked apart; carrier apps, system services without a Google Play listing and discontinued apps are left out. Apps from independent publishers pre-installed only on some phones (Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, Netflix, Office…) are ranked apart, as their download count is inflated.
  • Grade and score. VYLIA grid 3.0 · 505ed919, as in the app: permissions are judged by what the app is for (location costs nothing to a maps app, a lot to a game), trackers by their type.
  • Maximum exposure. Off the phone, nobody knows what you granted: every declared permission is counted as granted. On your phone, an app can get a better grade if you refuse access.
  • Trackers. Signatures found in the code by Exodus Privacy's static analysis, on the latest version published on Google Play. Their presence does not prove their activity, and an app can contain trackers Exodus does not know yet.
  • Limits. The target SDK is unknown (legacy storage access is counted); what the publisher does with data on its servers and security patterns are not measured. Exodus reports from 2021-08-09 to 2026-11-09; "old" flags a report more than a year old.
  • Data. The full details are published under the ODbL 1.0 licence in the VYLIA repository.
